story.title: Nvidia is investigating Jensen Huang’s relationship with a Chinese spy

facts.text: Nvidia’s board of directors announced Sunday that it’s launching an independent investigation following reports that CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a Chinese spy operation .

In response to earlier reports about the CEO’s relationship with Alice Huang, Nvidia had said that the pair’s interactions were “not unusual,” and that the company does not share classified information with customers.
As the AI race between the United States and China heats up , chips, especially Nvidia’s chips, have been a major focus .
“I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Jensen Huang wrote.
“To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me,” he said.

Multiple sources claim that a top executive at a Singapore AI firm suspected of steering Nvidia AI GPUs to China and who has close business ties with Jensen Huang was apparently passing information to Beijing as a Chinese intelligence asset.
According to The New York Times , U.S. intelligence has been aware of her activities for over a year already and has even briefed President Donald Trump on the situation.
However, Trump reportedly chose not to do anything about the information, as he apparently did not want to affect Nvidia sales or antagonize China.
“Megaspeed has been no different than many other regional cloud customers.

The suspect, Alice Huang or Huang Le, was listed as the managing director of Singaporean AI firm Megaspeed, an Nvidia cloud partner that builds data centers and rents out the compute to Chinese firms like Alibaba.
The investigation into the firm began when the U.S.
Commerce Department visited the firm’s Malaysia data center and found the Nvidia equipment that it ordered still packed in boxes.
This raised suspicion that the machines were either just shipped in or about to be shipped out, instead of being installed on the site.
Megaspeed was accused of helping smuggle $2 billion worth of Nvidia chips last year .
The Chinese embassy in Washington denied the allegations, saying that it was merely “groundless smears and slanders” against China.
Nevertheless, it would also make sense for Beijing to keep tabs on senior executives of the top American firms that arguably single-handedly fueled the AI boom.

Huang hasn’t yet been given a defensive briefing — a warning that U.S. counterintelligence agencies would sometimes give to American citizens who have been targeted by foreign intelligence services — even though the surveillance against Alice Huang continues.
The report speculates it is possible this was done to avoid alerting Alice Huang that she was being investigated.
Huang was spotted in public with the Nvidia chief.
She was photographed sitting beside Jensen Huang alongside other executives in an informal event around Computex 2024 in a LinkedIn post by NetThunder, identified as Megaspeed Chairwoman Alice Wong.

sources.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang may have been the target of a spy plot through 'Chinese intelligence asset,' report claims — exec from firm under investigation for smuggling banned AI chips to China accused of being a spy, was also feeding information to Beijing - Tom's Hardware
passages: Multiple sources claim that a top executive at a Singapore AI firm suspected of steering Nvidia AI GPUs to China and who has close business ties with Jensen Huang was apparently passing information to Beijing as a Chinese intelligence asset.
According to The New York Times , U.S. intelligence has been aware of her activities for over a year already and has even briefed President Donald Trump on the situation.
However, Trump reportedly chose not to do anything about the information, as he apparently did not want to affect Nvidia sales or antagonize China.
“Megaspeed has been no different than many other regional cloud customers.

The suspect, Alice Huang or Huang Le, was listed as the managing director of Singaporean AI firm Megaspeed, an Nvidia cloud partner that builds data centers and rents out the compute to Chinese firms like Alibaba.
The investigation into the firm began when the U.S.
Commerce Department visited the firm’s Malaysia data center and found the Nvidia equipment that it ordered still packed in boxes.
This raised suspicion that the machines were either just shipped in or about to be shipped out, instead of being installed on the site.
Megaspeed was accused of helping smuggle $2 billion worth of Nvidia chips last year .
The Chinese embassy in Washington denied the allegations, saying that it was merely “groundless smears and slanders” against China.
Nevertheless, it would also make sense for Beijing to keep tabs on senior executives of the top American firms that arguably single-handedly fueled the AI boom.

Huang hasn’t yet been given a defensive briefing — a warning that U.S. counterintelligence agencies would sometimes give to American citizens who have been targeted by foreign intelligence services — even though the surveillance against Alice Huang continues.
The report speculates it is possible this was done to avoid alerting Alice Huang that she was being investigated.
Huang was spotted in public with the Nvidia chief.
She was photographed sitting beside Jensen Huang alongside other executives in an informal event around Computex 2024 in a LinkedIn post by NetThunder, identified as Megaspeed Chairwoman Alice Wong.
